story: Ekalavya, a tribal prince, was turned away as a student by Drona. He made a clay statue of Drona and taught himself archery in front of it, until he was better than Arjuna. When Drona found out, he asked for Ekalavya's right thumb as his fee, and Ekalavya cut it off without hesitation.
belief: He is the great symbol of self-taught devotion and of the injustice of exclusion by birth. Many tribal communities honour him as a hero.
turns: He gave his thumb, and with it his future as the world's best archer, to a teacher who had refused to teach him.
facts: India's Eklavya Model Residential Schools for tribal students are named after him.
He learned to shoot again without his thumb.
Some versions say he later fought against Krishna and was killed by him.
lessons: Your devotion is precious; choose who receives it.
You can learn without anyone's permission.
more: He silenced a barking dog with seven arrows without hurting it, which revealed his skill to the princes.
He was the son of Hiranyadhanus, a chief of the Nishadas.
